page: Microsoft Azure E4-2ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 dedicated physical core via hyperthreading, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory density of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Local temporary storage is included via a bundled 161 GB SSD. There are no GPUs attached, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-threaded performance paired with low multi-core throughput due to the constrained two-vCPU footprint. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1630.0 (average) and a stress-ng single-core score of 1890.49. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics rank lower, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 1878.0, a PassMark CPU score of 2986.1, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 1933.27, all placing in the bottom tier relative to broader cloud hardware. Uncached memory bandwidth measured 14.31 GB/sec for reads and 13.48 GB/sec for writes.

Application benchmarks reflect the instance's high RAM-to-CPU ratio and limited parallel processing capabilities. Redis SET operations measured 2.02 million operations per second, while static web serving reached 3.53 GB/sec. Small-model LLM inference benchmarks achieved 131.97 tokens per second for prompt processing and 54.31 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter model. Instruction set support includes AVX-512 (AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI) along with hardware cryptography acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

This server architecture trades raw multi-core throughput for substantial memory capacity at an efficient footprint. The E4-2ds_v5 is suited for memory-intensive workloads that require low CPU core counts, such as caching tiers, in-memory key-value stores, intermediate data buffering, and lightweight relational databases where memory footprint matters more than parallel compute scaling.
description: Microsoft Azure E4-2ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs from a single physical Intel Xeon 8370C core running at 2.8 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM and 161 GB of local SSD storage. Designed with an x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides an elevated memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per thread, with hardware support for AVX-512, AES, and SHA-NI instructions. The server includes no GPUs and relies on virtualized networking without bundled public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark evaluations show balanced single-core throughput, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1630.0, but reduced overall multi-core performance due to its two-thread limit. Memory benchmarks reached 14.31 GB/sec read and 13.48 GB/sec write bandwidth on large uncached blocks, and Redis SET throughput achieved 2.02 million ops/sec. This configuration fits memory-heavy, low-parallelism workloads including caching services, small relational databases, and in-memory key-value layers.
